title: Nepal Bans Priyagold Biscuits After India Flags Cattle-Feed Bran
excerpt: Nepal halted imports, sales and distribution of Priyagold biscuits and ordered a recall of stocks after India's FSSAI suspended maker Surya Food and Agro's licence and moved to prosecute over alleged use of cattle feed bran.
body:
• Nepal has banned the import, sale and distribution of Priyagold biscuits made by India's Surya Food and Agro Ltd, describing the product as sub-standard in a notice issued on Monday, October 19.
  • India's food regulator, the FSSAI, has suspended the manufacturer's licence and initiated prosecution proceedings over the alleged use of cattle feed bran in biscuits meant for human consumption, alongside serious hygiene deficiencies found on inspection.
  • Authorised importers and food traders in Nepal have been told to recall existing stocks from the market immediately.
  • For shoppers: the product at issue is Priyagold biscuits manufactured by Surya Food and Agro Ltd in India — check the manufacturer name on the pack, and do not buy or eat packs covered by Nepal's recall while the case is pending.

Nepal has banned the import, sale and distribution of Priyagold biscuits manufactured by India's Surya Food and Agro Ltd, citing food safety concerns raised by India's own regulator. The Food Technology and Quality Control Department (FTQCD) announced the restrictions in a notice issued on Monday, describing the biscuits as sub-standard, according to LiveMint, reporting PTI.

What Nepal ordered

The department imposed the restrictions after an emergency meeting held virtually at the initiative of its director general, Sanjeev Kumar Karna. The notice said the decision was taken with human health security and consumer welfare in mind.

Traders, relevant organisations and consumers have been directed not to import the biscuits, and sales and distribution must stop. Authorised importers and food traders have also been instructed to recall existing stocks from the market immediately, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Nepal has not announced a separate inspection finding of its own; its stated rationale rests on the notice published by India's regulator.

The allegation in India

According to the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), an inspection of Surya Food and Agro revealed serious deficiencies in food safety and hygiene. The regulator has initiated legal proceedings for prosecution against the company over the alleged use of cattle feed bran in manufacturing Priyagold biscuits, along with other serious violations, and has suspended the manufacturer's licence.

Cattle feed bran is a by-product used in animal feed. The central allegation is that a material intended for animal consumption was used in biscuits intended for people. That allegation has not yet been finally determined in court, and the reports do not specify the quantity of biscuits affected, the number of retail outlets involved, or whether any illnesses have been linked to consumption of the product.

Why this matters beyond one brand

Priyagold is a mass-market biscuit brand, the kind sold in small packs at neighbourhood shops across India and in neighbouring markets. When a regulator in the country of manufacture suspends a licence and a neighbouring country then blocks imports on the basis of that notice, the case tests how quickly food-safety information travels across borders in South Asia — and how much shoppers in both countries learn about what was found.

For Indian families abroad, Priyagold packs also turn up in South Asian grocery stores. No recall in the United States was announced in the reports cited here, and Nepal's ban applies to Nepal. The practical check remains the same everywhere: read the manufacturer line on the pack. If it names Surya Food and Agro Ltd, treat the Nepal and FSSAI action as directly relevant to that product until regulators say otherwise.

What happens next

In Nepal, the immediate steps are the halt to imports and sales and the recall of stocks already on shelves. In India, the matter now sits with the legal proceedings FSSAI has initiated and with the suspended licence. Further action will depend on the regulatory process and any subsequent directions issued by the authorities in either country.

Surya Food and Agro's response was not included in the reports available at publication. If the company contests the findings, that defence — and any test results regulators publish — will determine whether the ban is a short interruption or the end of Priyagold's access to the Nepalese market.
